from itertools import combinations
from pysat.solvers import Glucose3

n = 8
edges = list(combinations(range(n), 2))
idx = {e:i+1 for i,e in enumerate(edges)}

def lit(i,j,color):
    v = idx[(min(i,j),max(i,j))]
    return v if color==1 else -v

s = Glucose3()
# no red K3
for tri in combinations(range(n),3):
    i,j,k = tri
    s.add_clause([lit(i,j,1),lit(i,k,1),lit(j,k,1)])
# no blue K4
for q in combinations(range(n),4):
    i,j,k,l=q
    s.add_clause([lit(i,j,0),lit(i,k,0),lit(i,l,0),lit(j,k,0),lit(j,l,0),lit(k,l,0)])

print(s.solve())
m=s.get_model()
sol=[1 if m[i]>0 else 0 for i in range(28)]
print(sol)
# verify
red=[e for e,i in zip(edges,sol) if i==0]
blue=[e for e,i in zip(edges,sol) if i==1]
redset=set(red); blueset=set(blue)
for tri in combinations(range(n),3):
    es=[tuple(sorted([a,b])) for a,b in combinations(tri,2)]
    if all(e in redset for e in es): print("red tri",tri)
for q in combinations(range(n),4):
    es=[tuple(sorted([a,b])) for a,b in combinations(q,2)]
    if all(e in blueset for e in es): print("blue k4",q)
print("ok")
